$comment: The 0SFS landing page's sky card background: square, filling the whole card, rendered by FOSS Earth with no interface (the website credits Google beside it). Framed by hand in the tuner (scripts/capture-scenes/tune.mjs): the eye is fixed over Georgian Bay, 400 km up, looking west-south-west as the Sun sets on the Earth's edge, an hour after the hero video's instant. The card's label and heading sit on the black sky above the edge, its text on the night side below. The exposure is metered, 2.3 stops darker than the meter's choice: from orbit the meter reads the night side below and settles on its floor, EV 1, so this shows the picture at EV 3.3, the air's band clipped white and the city lights visible. The lens flare (sky.exposure.lensFlare) gives the Sun its starburst and ghost reflections on a line through the picture's centre, reddened by the air. Tune with tune.mjs, or with --set, e.g. --set settings.renderer.exposureEV=-3 (lower is darker); compare exposures with --bracket=-2,-1,1,2.
name: sky-sunset-orbit
description: From 400 km above Georgian Bay, looking west-south-west at the Sun setting on the Earth's edge at 19:11:58 CDT on 25 October 2026, with the night side's city lights below.
